concepts.def: Stays at rest or constant velocity unless force acts

walkthroughs.body_html:
Speed = distance / time (scalar).

Velocity is speed with direction (vector).

1: object stays at rest or constant v unless force acts.

2: F = ma.

3: every action has equal and opposite reaction.

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.

mcqs.q: If a car has negative acceleration, what does that necessarily mean?
options: Negative acceleration means the car is moving backwards.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Negative acceleration always means the car is slowing down.
Its acceleration is in the negative direction (often opposite to the chosen positive direction); it may be slowing down or speeding up in reverse.

mcqs.q: When you push a wall, what does Newton's third law say about the wall?
options: The wall pushes back with a force proportional to how stiff it is, not equal to your force.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
The wall only pushes back if your force is strong enough to make it react.
The wall exerts an equal and opposite force on you at the same instant.
